note: The print_region table: stationery sizes by region, read by emitters/print.py through specs.py (rows appear there as print-<REGION>). Sizes are the usual national or ISO/ANSI sizes written from general knowledge, NOT read at a printer or standards page: every row is status U until a person reads the source. The bleed is a default, stated as printer-specific: the printer's own template wins.

print-EU.notes: UNVERIFIED. A4 and DL follow ISO 216 and ISO 269; 85 x 55 mm is the common European business card. The 3 mm bleed is a typical default, not a rule: ask the printer.

print-US.notes: UNVERIFIED. 3.5 x 2 in card, 8.5 x 11 in letter paper and the 9.5 x 4.125 in #10 envelope are the usual US sizes; the 0.125 in bleed is a typical default, not a rule: ask the printer.

print-JP.notes: UNVERIFIED. 91 x 55 mm is the usual Japanese business card, A4 is the office paper. Japanese post also uses the long-format envelopes (for example nagagata 3, 120 x 235 mm); DL is used here because the plan names DL and #10 only, so pass --envelope-mm for a local format. The 3 mm bleed is a typical default: ask the printer.
